To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) religion is an important factor in the formation of diasporas; (2) diaspora is an important factor shaping religion; (3) religion in diaspora is a dynamic process; (4) religion in diasporas is shaped by the interaction of religious and secular institutions; and (5) religion in diasparas can contribute to social cohesion, but also to conflict and exclusion.

The diaspora of a religion, like that of any other social group, is a dynamic, complex phenomenon, which cannot be understood without a close attention to the specific historical context of each case, and to the interplay between the global and the local.
